title: Validate IP Address
description: Given a string `queryIP`, return `"IPv4"` if it is a valid IPv4 address, `"IPv6"` if it is a valid IPv6 address, or `"Neither"` otherwise. A valid IPv4 address has 4 decimal segments `x1.x2.x3.x4` separated by `'.'`, where each `xi` is in `[0, 255]` with no leading zeros (except `"0"`). A valid IPv6 address has 8 hexadecimal segments separated by `':'`, where each segment has length 1 to 4 and consists solely of hex digits `0-9`, `a-f`, or `A-F`.
constraints: queryIP consists of English letters, digits, '.', and ':'.
hints: Check '.' and ':' counts or split preserving empty trailing segments (split(".", -1) in Java).
For IPv4 verify 1-3 ASCII digits, value <= 255, and no leading '0' when length > 1; for IPv6 verify length 1..4 and only hex characters.

examples.explanation: Four decimal octets in [0, 255] without leading zeros form a valid IPv4 address.
Eight groups of 1-4 hex digits form a valid IPv6 address.
256 exceeds the IPv4 octet upper bound of 255.
